act_descr: Act I — Spring Tide: Appetite and Discovery
chapters:
Negative Tide
    - March equinox king tide: predawn forage with Signe on a slick skerry off Saltholm; Alma tastes skær—brine like struck flint; second-person taste note ignites a childhood kitchen in Dragør.
    - Kitchen setup in the converted shipfitter’s hall on Refshaleøen; Kaspar frames NDAs and “IP around memory.” Mateo rigs a DIY salinity probe; Einar logs low tide windows; Freja maps pairings by shorelines.
    - May pop-up: “salted kohlrabi, skær, dill pollen.” Diners weep, call exes, leave voice memos; second-person interludes bloom with involuntary recall. Leif Ravn returns twice; anosmia thins only during skær course; writes a cryptic rave from his apartment above Torvehallerne.
    - Alma’s backstory flickers: blackout at Relæ, coins taped in knife roll, sleepwalking during menu changes, collecting forgotten napkins. She rejects dining-room tours, chases a star through saline gradients.
    - Kaspar installs an unlicensed recirculating skær tank in the basement fed by harbor water. Signe warns about permits, eelgrass beds, and won’t give coordinates; keeps her boundary tight.
    - Montage of Copenhagen: staff smokes in a Christianshavn alley; Kalvebod Fælled brackish ditches in late summer scouted early; winter routes past silent Paper Island flagged on a wall calendar. First hint of pressure: investor deck mentions Dubai.

The Backflush
    - August heatwave: harbor algae advisory; storm hits; tank pump backflushes; days later, fish die-offs, Islands Brygge harbor baths post sewage overflow alert. Second-person interludes sour—memories arrive jagged, intrusive.
    - Freja starts microdosing skær “to hear acidity,” nails pairings then doubles; a diner relives a crash mid-course and bolts; Fødevarestyrelsen inspection is quiet but real. Mateo refuses skær for pregnant guests; notes deviations in HACCP logs.
    - Signe, seeing torn eelgrass and trampled skerries near Saltholm from copycats, refuses to supply. Alma fabricates skær from kombu and salt to pause harvest; the decoy fails—VIP feels nothing and threatens a lawsuit over “withheld experience.”
    - Petra poaches Mateo and two servers, launches a lookalike dish with faux-skær; a blogger exposes her psilocybin hack; scandal splashes everyone. Kaspar spins it: “Only Alma’s is authentic memory cuisine.”
    - Einar films shredded eelgrass, dead pipefish, and the illegal tank; passes footage to Signe and a DTU Aqua postdoc at a rented lab bench in Lyngby. A city hearing opens at Teknik- og Miljøforvaltningen; Kaspar offers Einar a raise and title to bury the clips.
    - Alma serves skær to Ingrid at home, chasing one unbroken memory; they share ten lucid minutes—her father on the Dragør pier at dawn, herring buckets, wind-burned hands. The crash afterward agitates Ingrid; Alma breaks sobriety for one night, then returns raw, deciding to end it.
    - October reviewer cycle: Leif’s second review, a spare numbered list, calls the menu “a theft from a place that cannot consent.” Bookings surge anyway. Second-person interludes begin to question consent and scarcity as design.

Return
    - December staff exodus: Petra drains their line; Mateo comes back, ashamed; Freja’s dependence unspools; Einar pushes for catch limits. Winter service runs past mute Paper Island; awards dangle; Alma declines a TV spot.
    - January herring run: Alma and Signe track salinity and moon; Leif attends service with a pocket nebulizer, hearing taste words like notes that won’t resolve. February investor summit: Kaspar courts Dubai scouts; NDA culture hardens; inspectors circle.
    - Final spring tide under a supermoon: Alma, Signe, Mateo, Einar take a RIB to the Øresund Bridge skerry at negative tide; Petra’s team lurks on another boat. Alma harvests one last tuft, notes torn beds, says “enough.”
    - That night’s menu: a course called “Return”—eelgrass broth, cold smoke, no skær. Alma reads a one-page note on methods, damage, and limits; publishes coordinates and a moratorium; invites regulators to the pass. Second-person interludes shift to present tense: salt, steel, wind.
    - Kaspar pulls funding mid-service; half the room walks; the other half stays, tasting what’s left when spectacle is gone. Leif eats the no-skær menu; his smell does not return. He writes the final review anyway, full sense of absence as presence.
    - Coda: Municipal hearing concludes with fines, tank dismantled, shared stewardship plan led by Signe and DTU; Alma reopens smaller, no-tide-menu, staff paid through the pause. Ingrid’s moments of lucidity come now with simply salted rye and herring. Einar’s tide logs become the kitchen’s clock. Scarcity is no longer engineered—it is honored.
